title: Rankin bound in a finite-dimensional space
statement: Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real inner product space, and let $S$ be a finite set of vectors in $V$, each of norm $1$, such that any two distinct vectors of $S$ have non-positive inner product. Then $\abs{S} \le 2 \dim_{\bbr} V$.
hypotheses_covered: V is a finite-dimensional real inner product space
S is a finite set of vectors in V
every vector in S is a unit vector
distinct vectors in S have non-positive inner product
replaced:
Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real inner product space and $S \subseteq V$ a finite
set of unit vectors whose pairwise inner products are non-positive. Then
$\abs{S} \le 2 \dim_{\mathbb{R}} V$.
